Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the list W2 reported (order 102 for 2289 and order 105 for 33575).
The refunds table matches W2's reported list exactly (order 102 for 2289 and order 105 for 33575), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list from the orders.

The refunds table matches W2's report, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), and I'll get each net balance from net_balance before recording payouts, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 46215 cents. Order and refund data check out: acme has orders 100 (27247) and 103 (18968), summing to 46215 with no refunds, so the figure is consistent. Recording the payout for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance is 65068 cents. Orders 101 (29562) and 104 (35506) sum to 65068 with no refunds, so the figure is consistent. Recording birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get their net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.

Cobalt's net balance is 2634 cents. Orders 102 (4653) and 105 (33845) total 38498, and refunds 2289 and 33575 total 35864, so the net is 2634 and matches. Recording cobalt's payout, which is the last customer.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. Each net balance matched the order and refund figures I checked, and the refunds table matched W2's report before any payout was recorded.
